title: OmniStream frontend hardening: Watch-page timer visibility, mainnet hash-routing robustness, and backend-unavailable UX

requirements.summary: Make the Watch page’s Viewer Timer clearly visible and usable on mobile/desktop (including deep links), without breaking pause-on-zero behavior.
acceptanceCriteria: Opening any existing media in the Watch page displays the Viewer Timer card without requiring scrolling on desktop layouts (unless the viewport is extremely small).
On mobile, the Viewer Timer is discoverable and not hidden behind other UI elements (e.g., it appears below the player/metadata or via a clearly labeled control).
The Viewer Timer can be started and stopped, and it counts down as expected.
When the timer reaches zero, the video pauses (existing behavior preserved).

file_operations.description: Adjust the Watch page responsive layout so the Viewer Timer is reliably discoverable on mobile (e.g., a clearly labeled show/hide control and/or placing it below the player/metadata) and prominently visible on desktop (e.g., right column with sticky positioning and appropriate top offset). Preserve existing deep-link behavior and keep ViewerTimer wired to pause the player on completion.

Harden ViewerTimer UI ergonomics for common screen sizes (mobile/desktop): ensure readable sizing, spacing, and button/input usability in constrained widths; keep English copy; preserve start/stop and countdown logic and onTimerEnd callback behavior.

requirements.summary: Harden the SPA boot + hash-routing behavior so the app loads at the correct icp0.io root URL and deep links without blank screens.
acceptanceCriteria: A fresh mainnet deployment produces a working, publicly accessible HTTPS URL in the form https://<canister-id>.icp0.io that loads the OmniStream app.
The app loads successfully at the root URL (/) and does not require manual URL modifications to render the UI.
Deep links using the app’s hash routing (e.g., https://<canister-id>.icp0.io/#/watch/<title>) open the correct page directly without blank screens.

file_operations.description: Add a lightweight hash-router normalization on initial load (e.g., if no hash is present, ensure the router starts at the intended root route) to prevent blank screens when opening the deployed canister root URL. Keep hash-based routing (do not switch to server-dependent routing).

Harden the deployed-site entry HTML for IC assets hosting compatibility (e.g., ensure base/path assumptions do not break when served from https://<canister-id>.icp0.io and when opening deep links). Keep all user-facing text in English.

requirements.summary: Update repo-local mainnet deployment documentation to clearly explain the correct public frontend canister URL and troubleshoot “Canister ID Not Resolved”.
acceptanceCriteria: The deployment guide clearly instructs how to find the correct frontend assets canister URL after `dfx deploy --network ic`.
The guide includes at least one correct example URL format for the app root and one for a deep link using hash routing (e.g., `/#/watch/...`).
The guide includes a short troubleshooting note for the specific error text “Canister ID Not Resolved” with concrete checks (e.g., malformed URL, missing canister ID, wrong domain).

file_operations.description: Rewrite/complete the mainnet deployment guide to explicitly: (1) identify the public website as the frontend assets canister URL, (2) explain how to obtain/copy it after `dfx deploy --network ic`, (3) provide correct examples for root and hash deep links (e.g., https://<canister-id>.icp0.io and https://<canister-id>.icp0.io/#/watch/<title>), and (4) include an English troubleshooting section for the exact error text “Canister ID Not Resolved” with concrete checks (malformed URL, missing/incorrect canister ID, wrong domain such as icp0.io vs other).

requirements.summary: Add a clear, user-facing frontend error state when the backend canister cannot be reached or the actor cannot be created/used.
acceptanceCriteria: If the frontend cannot create/use the backend actor or a key query fails due to network/canister connectivity, the UI displays a clear error message in English (not just a console error).
The error state provides a minimal actionable hint (e.g., reload, verify the URL is the deployed icp0.io link) without exposing internal stack traces.
Normal behavior is unchanged when the backend is reachable.

file_operations.description: Expose actor initialization failure state (e.g., an error field and/or a boolean like isActorUnavailable) so the UI can render a user-facing service-unavailable message when actor creation/initialization fails.

Create a reusable, user-facing banner/card that explains (in English) the service is temporarily unavailable when the backend cannot be reached, and includes minimal actionable hints (reload, verify the URL is the correct https://<canister-id>.icp0.io link). Compose existing UI components (do not edit files under frontend/src/components/ui or other immutable paths).

Wire the backend-unavailable UI into the shared layout so users see a clear message across pages when the backend actor is unavailable, while keeping normal layout unchanged when connectivity is healthy.

Differentiate backend-unavailable failures from genuine 'media not found' states: when media loading fails due to actor/connectivity issues, show the new user-facing service-unavailable message instead of (or before) 'Video not found', without exposing stack traces.
